articles.title: NVIDIA CEO CHINESE SPY PROBE? Marco Rubio Responds To Reports Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
articles.description: WASHINGTON/PARIS — U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio addressed pressing global security matters in a media briefing prior to attending the G7 Ministerial meeting in France, declining to comment directly on reports of a classified intelligence memo involving Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Wang and Chinese espionage concerns while emphasizing that internal corporate probes remain separate from federal national security policy. Turning to Middle Eastern tensions, Rubio reaffirmed Washington’s military deterrence strategy regarding Iranian nuclear ambitions and maritime defense, characterizing Tehran’s diplomatic preconditions as “unacceptable”. The Secretary also outlined progress on post-conflict security architecture for Ukraine ahead of envoy talks in Abu Dhabi and warned the International Criminal Court (ICC) against asserting jurisdiction over non-member state personnel.

articles.title: Trump Eyes Major Meeting With Putin At China APEC Summit, Rubio Discusses Ukraine Security
articles.description: President Donald Trump expects to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin next week on the sidelines of the APEC Summit in China. The discussions are likely to cover major global issues, including nuclear disarmament and ending the war in Iran. Meanwhile, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended Trump’s approach towards Iran, warning that a nuclear-armed Tehran would pose a serious threat to global security. He said diplomatic progress with Iran remains unlikely due to its unrealistic demands. On Ukraine, Rubio highlighted progress in discussions on post-war security guarantees, with further talks expected in Abu Dhabi involving US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff. He also reaffirmed US support for a UN-backed mission to tackle gang violence in Haiti. Rubio declined to comment on Republican midterm election losses and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. He is visiting Paris from November 8–10 to attend the G7 foreign ministers’ meeting and advance US diplomatic interests.
